text: The 2021–22 season marked Liverpool Football Club's 130th season in existence and their 60th consecutive season in the top flight of English football. The club was on track to achieve a unique quadruple, securing a record-breaking ninth EFL Cup and winning the FA Cup by defeating Chelsea on penalties in both finals after each match ended in a goalless draw. However, they lost the Premier League title by just one point to Manchester City and, in a repeat of the 2018 final, were defeated by Real Madrid in the Champions League final. This season was the first since 2015–16 without Georginio Wijnaldum, who moved to Paris Saint-Germain, and the first since 2017–18 without Xherdan Shaqiri, who transferred to Lyon. Liverpool excelled in both the FA Cup and EFL Cup, beating Chelsea on penalties in both finals after goalless draws. On the final day of the season, Liverpool played Wolverhampton Wanderers at Anfield while Manchester City faced Aston Villa at the Etihad Stadium. Liverpool were down 0–1 early, but City were also a goal down to Villa. Sadio Mané equalized for Liverpool, keeping their title hopes alive as City were now 0–2 down. However, City scored three goals in five minutes to take the lead, and despite Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson scoring two late goals to win 3–1 against Wolves, Liverpool were denied the title by a single point. In the UEFA Champions League, Liverpool made history by becoming the first English club to win all six group stage matches, advancing to the final against Real Madrid, a rematch of the 2018 final. The final took place on 28 May 2022 in Paris, where Liverpool, who had previously faced Real Madrid in 1981, lost 0–1 as Vinícius Júnior scored the only goal. The club's spending was £36,000,000 in the summer and £37,500,000 in the winter, totaling £73,500,000. Their income was £45,050,000 in the summer and £1,500,000 in the winter, totaling £46,550,000, resulting in a net expenditure of £9,050,000 in the summer and £36,000,000 in the winter, amounting to £26,950,000 overall. On 12 July 2021, Liverpool announced a pre-season training camp in Austria featuring four friendlies. On 19 July, they confirmed completing their pre-season with two home friendlies. On 29 July, they confirmed a two-match training camp against Bologna in France between previously scheduled fixtures. Liverpool began the FA Cup in the third round at home to Shrewsbury Town and entered the competition in the third round. They entered the Champions League in the group stage, with the group draw held on 26 August 2021 and fixtures announced the next day. The round of 16 draw took place on 13 December 2021 in Nyon, Switzerland, with Liverpool facing Inter Milan. The quarter-final draw occurred on 18 March 2022, pairing Liverpool with Benfica. The semi-final draw followed on the same day, with Liverpool being drawn against Villarreal, the reigning Europa League champions. The final was held on 28 May 2022 in Paris, marking Liverpool's tenth European Cup final—the most of any English club—and their third in five years, repeating the 2018 final outcome. Players with no appearances are not included in the list. The monthly fan-voted award was given to the player chosen by fans voting on Liverpoolfc.com.
